articleTitle: Novel Highly Sensitive Photonic Sensor Using Dual Plasmonic Layers For Multiple Analyte Detection
abstract: The research introduces an External Metal Deposition (EMD) approach of novel Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) sensor operating in near to middle infrared spectrum. It utilizes the phenomenon of Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) to enhance the sensor performance as compared to other start-of-art Photonic Crystal Fiber sensors. Its novelty lies in its wide detection range of 1.35-1.41 Refractive Index Unit covering wide range of bio-chemical analytes. Its strong coupling efficiency and enhanced wavelength sensitivity equal to 30,000 nm/RIU and lowest sensor resolution of 3.33×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> Refractive Index Unit at an optimal gold thickness of 25 nm provides wider range of detection that broadens its application areas in biomedical, chemical, agricultural, pharmaceutical and food industries.

articleTitle: Q-switched Erbium-doped Fiber Laser with CeO2-PVA Film Saturable Absorber
abstract: Saturable absorbers (SAs) play a critical role in achieving Q-switched pulsed laser generation. This study investigated the potential of cerium oxide (CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) nanoparticles as SA material for erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) operations. A CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) film SA was carried out using a simple sonication process. The composite film exhibited nonlinear saturable absorption characteristics, enabling a stable Q-switched pulse generation in the EDFL cavity. The laser operated at a center wavelength of 1560 nm with various range of pulse duration (43.5 - 28.0 µs) with corresponding pump power from 32.0 to 47.8 mW and repetition rate ranging from 10.09 to 17.21 kHz.

articleTitle: Thresholding Methods in Rolling Shutter Camera-Based Optical Camera Communication
abstract: Optical camera communication (OCC) systems, which use light-emitting diodes as the transmitter and rolling shutter (RS) cameras as the receiver for high-speed communication, rely on received luminance for reliable data retrieval and face challenges due to the inherent nature of data collection. Additionally, efforts to make RS cameras compatible with low-speed mobile scenarios add further complexity to the system. Therefore, various methods have been proposed to address the diversity in pixel illumination values captured by the RS camera to ensure the system’s reliability. Here, we review the methods for RS camera-based OCC data decoding and discuss possiblefuture research directions.

articleTitle: Development of Sugar-Derived Water-Soluble Photoresist Materials with Potential for Environmental Impact Reduction and Biomaterial Applications
abstract: Conventional photoresist materials are generally coated and developed using organic solvents, but the water-soluble photoresist material in this study can be coated and developed using water. Patterning of water-soluble photoresist material on PMMA, which was contaminated or damaged by the organic coating solvent and developer in the conventional photoresist material, resulted in the fabrication of 6 µm holes and 3 µm lines. The water-based coating and development process is expected to contribute to biomaterial applications and environmental impact.

articleTitle: The Effect of Hygroscopic Coating in FBG’s Sensitivity and Linearity Improvement
abstract: Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors are optical fiber sensors that utilize Bragg gratings imprinted in the core of the fiber to detect changes in temperature, strain, vibration, and other parameters. This paper explores coating an FBG with zinc oxide nanostructures synthesized using a hydrothermal method with hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) to enhance its humidity sensing performance. The ZnO-HMT coating increases the hygroscopicity and humidity sensitivity of the FBG sensor. Experimental results demonstrate the coated FBG has a humidity sensitivity of 0.002nm/%RH compared to 0.00009nm/%RH for an uncoated FBG across a 40-80%RH range. The ZnO-HMT coated FBG also has a 92% linearity. Scanning electron microscopy reveals the ZnO-HMT coating has a porous, island-like nanostructure on the FBG which aids water vapor adsorption. The coating causes an initial conditioning effect, requiring pre-exposure to stabilize the sensitivity over humidity cycles. Overall, the ZnO-HMT coated FBG shows significantly improved sensitivity and reliable response after conditioning, confirming that hygroscopic coatings can enhance FBG performance for humidity sensing.

articleTitle: Heptylamine Plasma Polymerization Immobilization SPR Biosensor for Glucose
abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCD) such as diabetes affects 18.3% of the Malaysian adult population. Non-invasive optical methods and biosensors to detect glucose levels will encourage more diabetic screening to be undertaken by the general population. In this work, we experimentally demonstrated a glucose biosensor by immobilizing glucose oxidase (GOx) by cross-linking via glutaraldehyde (GA) on plasma polymerized Heptylamine films (HApp) using the Kretschmann-based surface plasmon resonance (K-SPR) method. Our findings confirmed an average sensitivity of 5.70°/M for detecting glucose levels ranging from 8 mM to 20 mM at 785 nm. This study contributes to early detection of diabetes via optical biosensing, plasma polymerization and enzyme immobilization techniques.

articleTitle: Chlorophyll-based Saturable Absorber for Q-switched Pulse Generation in Er-Doped Fiber Laser Cavity
abstract: In this paper, we present experimental results on the use of all-organic Chlorophyll-based saturable absorber (Chl-SA) extracted from spinach for the generation of Q- switched pulse. The Chl-SA was fabricated by depositing Chl in powder form onto a fiber ferrule. The Chl-SA generated Q- switched pulse at 1559-1560 nm when employed in a 980 nm laser diode pumped erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) cavity. Pulse generation was achieved from 45 mW pump power up to 70 mW pump powers where the repetition rate increased while pulse duration shortened with increasing pump power. The highest repetition rate of 15.15 kHz and shortest pulse width of 32 µs were obtained. This highlights the promising potential of chlorophyll as a standalone material and its capacity to potentially boost the generation of pulse lasers when combined with other materials.

articleTitle: Functional Confirmation of AWG-Based Wavelength Routers in Recursive Wavelength Routing Networks
abstract: Wavelength routing domain structure that uses AWG-based wavelength routers in recursive configuration is proposed. Then, it discusses the inside router connection matrix, scalability of proposed structure by analyzing several features and application area size. Results showed the feasibility of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Thickness Dependent Absorption Properties of Molybdenum Gallium Carbide Saturable Absorber for Pulsed Fibre Laser Generation
abstract: The thicknesses of molybdenum gallium carbide (Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C) MAX phase saturable absorbers (SAs) significantly affect their potential as vital photonics devices to generate high- power and energetic non-linear optical pulses for multi-disciplinary fibre laser applications. In this work, the thicknesses of Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C SAs fabricated through solution casting technique with five different concentrations are numerically analysed and practically validated by using MATLAB and 3D measuring laser microscopy, respectively and incorporated into Q-switched and mode-locked erbium-doped fibre laser (EDFL). The numerical and experimental thicknesses of Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C SAs are ideally decreased with increasing concentration. The 0.500 wt.% Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C SA with an actual thickness of 6.910 μm is revealed to have the best performance in both Q-switched and mode-locked EDFL.

articleTitle: Efficient Brillouin frequency shift extraction method employing Brillouin gain spectrum fitting in the distributed BOTDA fiber sensor
abstract: This paper demonstrates the deployment of quadratic curve fitting (QCF) based on half-peak Brillouin gain spectrum (BGS) for fast and accurate Brillouin frequency shift (BFS) extraction. The method was analysed and compared with three other methods such as Lorentzian curve fitting (LCF), Gaussian curve fitting (GCF) and pseudo-Voigt curve fitting (pVCF). The QCF based on half-peak achieved an accuracy similar to other curve fitting methods. In addition, the QCF has a faster processing time by eight-fold than the others, allowing the system to handle a large amount of data with good performance. The results would provide some general ideas for deploying the QCF algorithm for the system on chip platform with direct detection for fast BFS measurement.

articleTitle: Photonic Crystal Based MMI Design Using Silicon Nitride for Wavelength Division (De)multiplexing
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact multimode interferometer using 2D photonic crystals. The proposed device is realized on a silicon nitride platform for fabrication flexibility and its advantageous intrinsic properties. The device is optimized and designed using the finite-difference time-domain method to (de)multiplex 1550 nm and 1310 nm wavelengths. The footprint of the proposed device is 20 µm × 7.5 µm, and the lowest insertion loss and crosstalk are 0.36 dB and -16.23 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Making Quantum Key Distribution a Commodity: The All-Silicon Approach
abstract: The dawning of the quantum age makes quantum key distribution (QKD) an indispensable necessity for our global communication infrastructure. The realization of an all-silicon QKD transmitter supplied by a light source that is native to silicon integration platforms is seen as a disruptive step towards the pervasive introduction of QKD in new applications, which up to now have not been explored due to the missing credentials of quantum optics as a cost-effective and highly miniaturized technology.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fiber Optic-Based Hand Tool Vibrations Detection and Classification Using Long Short-Term Memory Network
abstract: This work proposes an effective method to detect and classify hand tool vibrations using a deep learning-based fiber optic sensing technique. The MFCCs are used as features to train a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to classify the hand tools. The classification outcome demonstrated a considerably good average precision score of at least 70%. This indicates that the proposed MFCC-LSTM-based Fiber optic sensing method has great potential for detecting and classifying hand tools.

articleTitle: UV-Curing TiO2-SiO2 Gas-Permeable Mold Material for Nanofabrication by Nanoimprint Lithography-Injection Molding Hybrid Technology
abstract: In this study, UV-curing gas-permeable mold material was developed that can improve gas entrapment during fabricating, which is a challenge in nanoimprint lithography (NIL). An advanced nanofabrication technology that hybridizes the high-resolution of NIL with the mass productivity of injection molding has enabled nanofabrication of polypropylene with a height of 300 nm and a base diameter of 240 nm. This technology enables nanofabrication of plastics with short cycle times, and is expected to create functional surfaces such as antibacterial through nanofabrication.

articleTitle: Computational modeling of random photonic networks for sensing applications
abstract: We present a computational model for random photonic networks consisting of micro-scale optical waveguides. For these networks, we calculate the scattering matrices and internal field distributions. To demonstrate the potential of the networks as sensing devices, we simulate the trajectory of a scattering matrix pole in response to a local network perturbation.

articleTitle: Dual-bidirectional SOAs for the generation of Multiwavelength Fiber Laser based on Lyot Filter
abstract: This work demonstrated a performance of multiwavelength fiber laser which generating 90 of lasing lines with a wide extinction ratio of 40 dB. This MWFL also provides broad L-band wavelength of 18 nm ranging from 1602 nm to 1620 nm. The experiment configuration consists of a dual-bidirectional semiconductor optical amplifier (SOAs) which consist of booster optical amplifier (BOA) and linear semiconductor optical amplifier (LSOA), a Lyot filter, and a polarization maintenance fiber length of 30 m. A combination of polarization controller and polarization-dependent isolator contributes a nonlinear polarization rotation effect and produces a stable and flat multiwavelength spectrum. With the alteration of HWP angle, the flatness of MWFL is degraded.

articleTitle: Study of Equalization Enhanced Phase Noise in EDFA-Amplified Optical Communication Systems
abstract: The significant influence of equalization enhanced phase noise on the performance of long-haul EDFA-amplified optical fiber communication systems has been investigated in this paper. A 128-Gbaud DP-16QAM multi-channel 2400 km Nyquist-spaced optical transmission system has been considered, with the application of the electronic dispersion compensation and the digital nonlinearity compensation schemes.

articleTitle: 5G RoF Dense Network Design Based on Optical Heterodyne Technique
abstract: This work analyses a 5G dense urban cellular network using optical heterodyne technique with the aim to design multi-band scenario of two layers network. The proposed network consists of two different optical carriers representing macrocell of 4 GHz and microcell of 30 GHz radio frequency. The target radio frequency has been achieved utilizing dual sideband optical carrier suppression method by using CW laser and LiNb MZM. For separating the two optical signals at the receiving end a delay interferometer has been used. The system performance has been demonstrated in terms of bit error rate and receiver quality factor. The results shows that the power penalty for 4 GHz and 30 GHz is 0.8 dB and 1.1 dB respectively between 0 km and 10 km lines at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> where the system can achieve error free transmission.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic Generation of Thermally Poled Silicon Germanium Oxide Films Deposited by ICPCVD
abstract: An inductively coupled plasma chemical vapor deposition (ICPCVD) technology was used to deposit a silicon germanium oxide (SiGeO) film on fused silica (FS), and thermal poling was applied to it. It was found that at a higher poling temperature, this sample could produce a stronger second harmonic generation (SHG) signal than FS under the same poling conditions. The development of this nonlinear optical material will help develop high-performance, low-cost silicon photonic devices.

articleTitle: Enhanced Oxygen Sensing with Surface Plasmon Resonance Optical Fiber
abstract: This study demonstrates a technique to enhance oxygen concentration detection by integrating surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and fluorescence-based sensors using multi-mode plastic optical fiber (POF). The optical sensor unit comprises silver with surface plasmon resonance properties and organic dye indicators, primarily focusing on fluorescence dyes, specifically Tris (4,7-diphenyl-1,10-phenanthroline) ruthenium (II) dichloride Ru(dpp)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/[Ru(dpp)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>. The analysis involved analyzing the sensing capabilities of POF coated with [Ru(dpp)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and ${\text{Ag}}/\left[ {\operatorname{Ru} {{({\text{dpp}})}_3}{{^1}_2}^ + } \right.$ in intensity changes and wavelength shift, respectively. The emission spectra of [Ru(dpp)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> showed a peak at 602 nm, and the emission intensity decrased as the oxygen content increased. Incorporatiing SPR revealed a reduction is emission intensity and a leftward wavelength shift with increasing oxygen content. The result demonstrates that ${\text{Ag}}\left[ {{\text{Ru(dpp}}{{\text{)}}_{\text{3}}}{{^{\text{1}}}_{\text{2}}}^{\text{ + }}} \right.$ has great slope of the series with 0.0589 and [Ru(dpp)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> has slope of 0.0099.

articleTitle: Graphene Oxide based Passive Saturable Absorber Embedded in Chitin and PVA: A Comparison
abstract: This research demonstrated a Q-switched Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser (EDFL) using graphene oxide (GO) film fabricated via a modified Hummer’s method from graphite flakes as the saturable absorber (SA). The GO was separately embedded with two host polymers; polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitin. The difference in the host polymer was compared in terms of the SAs’ performances. In the same range of pump power, the GO-chitin produced a pulse repetition rate of up to 91.17 kHz while GO-PVA operated at 1530.4 nm with 80.06 kHz of maximum repetition rate. The signal to noise ratio (SNR) at maximum pump power were 49.37 dB and 50.10 dB for GO-Chitin and GO-PVA, respectively. This work contributes to the understanding of how host polymer matrices affect the efficiency of SAs in fiber lasers, with implications for the advancement of laser technology in various industrial and scientific applications.

articleTitle: High solar-energy density induction in semiconductor nano-antennas
abstract: This work aims to investigate the harvesting of high solar-energy density using semiconductor nano-antennas through active control based on modulated optical pumping. By manipulating the effective susceptibility of semiconductor nanomaterials through carrier density modulation based on an intensity-modulated optical pump, we aim to design semiconductor nano-antennas with dispersion features that are ultra-responsive to sunlight, which enables an efficient trapping, amplification, and storage of sunlight. We achieve this through a precise tuning of the pump-intensity modulation frequency, which governs the modulation frequency of the electrical susceptibility of the nanoantenna for the optimal trapping of sunlight. Our results are based on numerical simulations that reflect theoretical and experimental findings.

articleTitle: Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) Spectroscopy for Leptospira DNA Detection
abstract: Surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy is a promising biomolecule detection technique. In this work, we analyzed the vibrational modes from leptospira deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). The metallic nanoparticles (NPs) were chemically functionalized to enable probe DNA (pDNA) immobilization. Successful hybridization between pDNA to the complementary DNA (cDNA) sequence was verified by high Ra-man characteristics of phosphate backbone (${\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_{2 - }}$) and adenine-thymine (A-T) bases pair. The finding shows the potential used of SERS spectroscopy as alternative diagnostic method for leptospirosis disease.

articleTitle: Metal-organic Framework Plasmonic Sensor for Methylthioninium Chloride Detection

authors.preferredName: Wan Mohd Ebtisyam Mustaqim Mohd Daniyal

abstract: In this work, an optical sensor based on a surface plasmon resonance sensor (SPR) is developed for methylene blue compound detection, utilising a metal-organic framework as the sensing medium. Zeolitic-imidazolate frameworks (ZIF-8) were used as a sensing material to improve the SPR sensor’s performance in detecting methylene blue compounds. SPR results showed a good sensitivity of 1.3821 °ppm-1 for methylene blue sensing when ZIF-8 was integrated as a sensing material. This is due to the additional active sites provided by ZIF-8 for the adsorption of methylene blue compound. The detection limit (LOD) and quantification limit (LOQ) were reported as 0.92 ppm and 2.79 ppm, respectively. Nevertheless, the sensitivity of the SPR sensor declined beyond 1 ppm methylene blue concentration due to the fully occupied active sites of ZIF-8, which limit further interaction with the methylene blue compound.

articleTitle: Liquid Film Temperature Measurement Methods Based on Active Laser Absorption Spectroscopy: A Review
abstract: This paper reviews the liquid film temperature measurement methods based on optical techniques, and discusses the basic principles, advantages, and application scenarios of non-contact active temperature measurement methods, including Raman Scattering, Planar Laser Induced Fluorescence and Laser Absorption Spectroscopy temperature measurement, for liquid films.

articleTitle: E-Band Signal Amplification in "Waterless" Thulium-Doped Fibers: Numerical Analysis
abstract: A fiber-optic amplifier module incorporating a parallel configuration of two thulium-doped (TM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>) fibers (TDFs) has been designed and presented in this paper. An aspect of E-band (1360 nm to 1460 nm) signal amplification is achieved in the "waterless" TDFs which renders broadband and high gain in the output signal. The amplifier module’s performance has been evaluated via numerically optimizing the TDFA’s geometric and physical parameters. An average gain of 37.12 dB and a noise figure of <3.93 dB have been obtained in the wavelength region of 1412 nm to 1460 nm with a maximum of 41.54 dB at 1432 nm having moderately uniform gain. Utilizing the optimized parameter set, the percentage increase of 0.029% and decrease of 0.043% in signal gain at the wavelength 1420 nm and 1448 nm have been obtained respectively inculcating the nonlinear ion-ion interaction mechanism (IM) effects.

articleTitle: 1.56 µm of Dissipative Soliton Resonance Utilizing Alpha-Phase Aluminum Oxide Saturable Absorber
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a dissipative soliton resonance effect utilizing alpha-phase aluminum oxide as a mode-locker. The generated laser operated at 1.56 µm, showing a broadening effect from 14.8 to 56.3 ns within 25 to 142 mW pump power. Up to 15.48 mW output power and 1.33 nJ pulse energy were measured at maximum pump power without any trace of wave-breaking effect. This work will pave the way of aluminum oxide family’s exploration for nanosecond laser applications in the near future.

articleTitle: Enhanced Visualisation of Plant Water Uptake Network Using Fluorescent Carbon Dots
abstract: This study investigates the application of carbon dots (CDs) for visual enhancement of the plant’s vascular system. The synthesised CDs were fed to Vigna radiata plants to facilitate the uptake of CDs into the vascular system. A custom-built microscope setup featuring a colour sCMOS camera was developed for widefield reflectance and fluorescence imaging. Our results reveal a notable fluorescence signal emitted by the CDs within the xylem tubes, significantly enhancing the visualisation of the vascular system. This study highlights the potential of CDs as a valuable label for studying plant physiology.

articleTitle: A High-quality Factor Ring Resonator-based Refractive Index Sensor for the Detection of Tuberculosis Disease
abstract: The presented work examines the detection of tuberculosis disease (TB) using a ring resonator-based refractive index sensor (R.I). The R.I of the infected blood with TB is sensed in the C-Band. The parameters are optimized to improve the sensitivity parameter using Lumerical VarFDTD. The proposed sensor has accomplished a sensitivity of 400 nm/RIU and the highest quality factor of 1154.04 is achieved for highly affected patient TB4.

articleTitle: Optical Microbottle Resonator Cavity Alteration with High Precision CO2 Laser
abstract: A method in altering the microcavity of a whispering gallery mode (WGM) microbottle resonator (MBR) is reported with the utilization of high precision CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. The altered MBR cavity shows beneficial spectral features with clear WGM transmission dips of 20 dB. Even with increased surface roughness due to the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser ablation process, high Q optical resonances 105 were generated by the altered MBR.

articleTitle: Optical Hyperuricemia Sensor with Uricase Biofunctionalized Stacked Nanocomposite
abstract: This paper presents an advanced optical sensor based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) designed to detect hyperuricemia, characterized by elevated uric acid (UA) levels. The sensor features a stacked nanocomposite comprising gold-graphene quantum dots (GQD) biofunctionalized with uricase enzyme, ensuring high sensitivity and selectivity for UA detection over other potentially competing interferents like ascorbic acid, glucose, D-cystine, urea, and creatinine commonly found in biological samples. The developed sensor achieves an impressive sensitivity of 0.093°/(mg/dL) for UA at 12 mg/dL, significantly higher than the recorded sensitivity of 0.015°/(mg/dL) for all other potential interferents at the same concentration. This highlights the sensor’s exceptional precision in discerning UA. Moreover, the sensor demonstrates notable selectivity for UA even at low concentrations, registering a resonance angle shift of 0.371° at 0.5 mg/dL, compared to a lower angle shift of 0.185° for other interferents at higher concentrations of 12 mg/dL. These findings emphasize the sensor’s accuracy and rapid response in distinguishing UA, positioning it as a promising tool for early diagnosis and management of hyperuricemia in clinical settings, addressing a critical need for reliable and efficient UA detection.
